title: Each viewer sees only what the operator allows
description: Serves "They see only what they may."; "Access is enforced everywhere.". One access rule, apart from how the collection is organised (D-124), decides what each account may see. JS-186 introduces the rule; this task gives it its full content. Configuration and invitations (JS-192) set it.
acceptanceCriteria: Configuration sets, for an account, a rating ceiling, allowed sets of titles and exceptions; a show's rule reaches its seasons and episodes, so a missing mark on a season never hides or shows its episodes by surprise.

TestAccess gains a restricted viewer: every route that names a title answers as for an unknown one and sends no byte, on api and on stream; every list, search, count, Continue watching, next episode and collection holds no such title (named mutant: the stream role skipping the check).
Forced: a title is hidden from a viewer mid-film; their next segment and byte range, through another replica, are refused (the outage exception is DOMAINS 37's).
An administrator sees everything; a hidden title's watch state stays stored and is not shown.
A collection or way in never counts or reveals a hidden member, and no way of organising titles grants anything (D-124).
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.
